title: Metals - 123 school
heading: Metals
intro: Test your knowledge by typing your answer and comparing it with the correct answer. Then click 'Check answers'.

questions.q: Name three properties that most metals have
questions.a: For example: shiny, good conduction of heat and electricity, deformable (malleable and ductile), high density, solid at room temperature

questions.q: Which metal is liquid at room temperature?
Why are copper wires used in electricity cables?
questions.a: Copper conducts electricity very well and is easy to shape

questions.q: What is an alloy?
questions.a: A mixture of a metal with one or more other substances (usually other metals as well)

questions.q: What is bronze made of?
What is brass made of?
What is steel made of?
questions.a: Iron with a small amount of carbon (and sometimes other metals)

questions.q: Why do people sometimes make an alloy instead of using a pure metal?
questions.a: The alloy has better properties, for example it is harder or rusts less quickly

questions.q: What is the metal in stainless steel that prevents rusting?
What forms when magnesium burns?
Balance: Mg + O<sub>2</sub> → MgO
Balance: Fe + O<sub>2</sub> → Fe<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub>
questions.a: 4 Fe + 3 O<sub>2</sub> → 2 Fe<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub> (left 4 Fe and 6 O, right 4 Fe and 6 O)

questions.q: Balance: Al + O<sub>2</sub> → Al<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub>
questions.a: 4 Al + 3 O<sub>2</sub> → 2 Al<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub> (left 4 Al and 6 O, right 4 Al and 6 O)

questions.q: Balance: Cu + O<sub>2</sub> → CuO
Balance: Zn + HCl → ZnCl<sub>2</sub> + H<sub>2</sub>
Balance: Na + H<sub>2</sub>O → NaOH + H<sub>2</sub>
questions.a: 2 Na + 2 H<sub>2</sub>O → 2 NaOH + H<sub>2</sub> (left 2 Na, 4 H and 2 O, right 2 Na, 4 H and 2 O)

questions.q: Which gas forms when sodium reacts with water?
What is rust?
questions.a: Iron oxide, which forms when iron reacts with oxygen and water

questions.q: What is needed for iron to rust?
Name two ways to protect iron from rusting
questions.a: For example: painting, a layer of zinc (galvanising), a layer of oil or grease, another metal layer (chromium plating), an alloy such as stainless steel

questions.q: What is galvanising?
questions.a: Covering an iron object with a layer of zinc

questions.q: Why does aluminium not rust through?
questions.a: A thin, dense layer of aluminium oxide forms on the surface and protects the metal

questions.q: What is an ore?
questions.a: A rock from which you can extract a metal

questions.q: Which metal is made from iron ore in the blast furnace?
What is carbon (coke) used for in the blast furnace?
questions.a: Coke (carbon) removes oxygen from the ore. It also supplies heat.

questions.q: What is the iron that comes out of the blast furnace called?
Why is recycling metals important?
questions.a: It saves raw materials and energy, and there is less waste

questions.q: Which metals are attracted by a magnet?
A piece of copper has a mass of 89.6 g and a volume of 10.0 cm³. What is the density of copper?
A block of aluminium has a volume of 40 cm³. The density of aluminium is 2.7 g/cm³. What is the mass?
A piece of iron of 156 g has a density of 7.8 g/cm³. What is the volume?
Which metal has the greatest density: aluminium (2.7 g/cm³), iron (7.9 g/cm³), lead (11.3 g/cm³) or zinc (7.1 g/cm³)?
An ore of 200 g contains 140 g of iron oxide (Fe<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub>). What is the mass percentage of iron oxide in the ore?
500 g of ore contains 8.0 mass% of copper. How many grams of copper are there in the ore?
What is the symbol of lead?
Which of these metals occurs in nature mainly as an ore and not in pure form: gold or iron?
questions.a: Iron, because iron reacts easily with oxygen; gold occurs in pure form
